notes: Call with Dana Whitfield on the 240-seat renewal. She opened with a 'special' 5% off that had to be signed within 48 hours. Offered to commit to 300 seats; she came back at 6% and said anything more needed sign-off from her director.

I emailed their VP of Sales directly about the Q3 add-on. Dana replied within the hour, visibly annoyed, and the revised quote came back at just 4% off list ($466k). Whole thing felt like we got pushed back to square one.

Shared the PipelineIQ proposal ($391k for equivalent modules). Dana went to Raj Menon (Regional Sales Director) and we had 19% off within two days, $393.7k annual. Raj said the 'special' expired only 'if we hadn't been in touch', so the 48-hour clock was theatre.
Added a second quote from a different vendor and asked for 21%. Raj approved on the call, $384k. Dana said it was a good thing we asked early.

Northwind was acquired by Stratus Group in April; Raj has left and a new VP Revenue Operations (Alan Pierce) is now signing discounts. Rival quote only got us 10% since Alan wanted to 'align to group pricing guidelines'. He asked for a follow-up in Q3 once the integration settles.
Alan Pierce took the rival quote seriously after we gave him the full line-item comparison. 18% off, $398.5k annual. Regional Sales Director role no longer exists on their org chart.
Proposed a 3-year deal to Tomas Brandt for 18% off. He agreed to 5% only if we accepted a 7% annual price escalator. Walked away; the escalator would have wiped out the savings by year 3.
Let the quarter run and signed on June 27. Tomas sent a revised quote on June 26 at 15% off, $265.2k, without us pushing. He admitted they were 'about $2M light' for Q2.
Mentioned a rival quote at the start of October, right after quarter began. Tomas held at 7% and said Lena Kruger (VP Sales Ops) had 'no flexibility until the numbers close'. Parked until December.
Waited until Dec 29, revised quote arrived with 17% off ($259k) the day before I planned to call. Lena Kruger approved at the end-of-year review; Tomas copied her on the thread.

Same pattern again, a revised quote landed March 27 at 18% off list for the add-on seats ($255.8k). Tomas apologised for the 'late-quarter scramble'. We are comfortable that late March is the sweet spot.

Mentioned two rival bids on the Chicago-Dallas lanes. Gudrun Halvorsen went quiet for a week and returned with a 3% lane reduction and a note that spot capacity 'is tight in July'. Relationship noticeably cooler.

Committed to 85 loads per week on the core lanes for 12 months. Gudrun brought in Soren Lindqvist (Director of Network Planning) and he approved 12% off the lane rates, about $148.8k annualised savings. Fuel surcharge table unchanged.
Raised the weekly commitment to 110 loads on the Midwest corridor. Soren signed off 14% on those lanes within a day. Gudrun noted the committed tonnage 'let us staff the dedicated tractors'.
Asked for net-45 instead of net-30 in return for a rate cut. Gudrun gave a flat 6% but said terms are corporate policy. Rates moved less than volume did last time.

Soren is now handling renegotiation himself after Gudrun moved to the Pacific region. Committed 125 loads weekly through Q2 2027; 15% off lanes, which is the best Halvorsen rate on record. Soren wants quarterly volume reports.
Offered 40,000 TEU-equivalents annual volume. Kenji Okafor added a minimum charge per sailing that cancelled out the rate cut, net about 1% savings. We declined.
Offered to pay net-10 rather than net-45. Kenji took it to the CFO, Ananya Rao, who approved 9% off the base rate ($80.5k). Kenji said their working-capital line is 'what keeps me up at night'.
Dropped a competitor's number on the Shanghai-LA lane. Kenji said it was not comparable and offered 2%. Ananya was not looped in.
Went to net-7 via early-pay platform for a 12% rate reduction ($107k). Ananya approved in a single email. Kenji joked that if the platform fee is ours, 'we have a deal'.
Tried one more time with a firm 50k TEU commitment. Same minimum-charge clause reappeared (now $140 per empty sailing). Kenji said volume on its own was not what drove their pricing.
Pushed Rhys Calloway at quarter-end. He said the LME index moved up 3% that week and refused anything below the index plus premium. Gave 2% on freight only.
Offered a 36-month supply agreement for 4,200 tonnes per year. Rhys escalated to Priscilla Hartmann (CCO) who approved 12% off premium over LME. Said she needs contract certainty to justify hedging.
Cited a Turkish mill quote. Rhys agreed to 4% on the spot component and left the premium alone. Priscilla not involved.
Extended to a 48-month term with an index collar. Priscilla Hartmann signed 14% off the premium, $301k a year. Best figure Kestrel has given us to date.
Quarter-end ask again. Rhys said Q2 was already booked and that nothing changes because of the calendar. 3% on freight consolidation only.
Offered net-15 for lower resin pricing. Ilse Verhoeven said credit insurance already covers extended terms and prompt pay 'is not a lever'. Got a 2% courtesy cut.
Committed 1,800 tonnes of HDPE, got 6% on that grade only. Ilse suggested adding other grades but we didn't have them in scope.
Bundled HDPE, masterbatch and stretch film packaging into one PO. Head of Commercial Stefan Brouwer approved 16% across the basket, $236.8k. Ilse said it was 'the cleanest deal we've done'.
Added PP copolymer to the bundle. Stefan matched with 17% on the whole basket, which equals the best offer on file. Quote returned within 36 hours.
Wrote to the CEO to speed up a contract. Stefan took over from Ilse and gave 8% but made it clear he would have done the bundle at 16% if we'd simply asked.
Told Fiona McBride we had a bid from a Vietnam EMS provider. She said 'we do not compete on price against offshore' and offered 3% on NRE. Sent nothing in writing.

Our VP Ops called Aldercrest COO Bernard Tashkent directly. By Friday we had a 'strategic partner' rate of 18% off the unit price on the 3 SKU family ($594k). Fiona said she'd been kept out of the loop.
Asked for net-60 to net-30 trade. Fiona offered 5% and said payment terms are a 'finance conversation'. Not worth repeating.
Second exec-to-exec call with Bernard on the new line. 20% off, which is Aldercrest's best known number. Fiona was copied on the thread but said nothing.
Volume commitment of 120k units. Fiona gave 7% and said the COO's office 'would have to bless anything bigger'. We didn't re-escalate.
Bernard's chief of staff, Hye-jin Park, now coordinates. Call got scheduled within 24 hours and 17% was approved a week later. Process is a little slower than before but still works.
Tried bundling NRE tooling and unit pricing. Joao Almeida said Sintra's accounting keeps these separate and quoted 2% only. Plant GM Luis Ferreira not in the call.
Let the quote sit until Sept 24. Joao called with a 14% offer on the PCBA line because Luis Ferreira had open capacity in October. $246.4k saved annually.
Mentioned a rival quote; Joao shrugged and offered 6%. The real movement only came at the quarter end, which we did not use.
Pushed ahead to the last week of March. Luis Ferreira personally approved 16% off, citing a cancelled order from another customer. This is their floor as far as I can tell.
Same play in Sept. 15% with a 4-week lead time, signed Sept 25. Joao says the plant reviews utilisation weekly in the final month.
Went above Marguerite Doyle to the Operations Director on the janitorial contract. Marguerite reacted sharply and the final offer was 4%. She would not take our calls for two weeks.

Combined janitorial, security and grounds across three sites into one agreement. Marguerite and Pete Ostrowski (Regional Operations Director) approved 17% off ($108.8k). They asked us to add landscape as a bonus.
Added two more buildings; Marguerite gave 7% on the extra scope only.
Extended bundle with pest control and window cleaning. Pete signed 19% off the combined $640k base. Marguerite is leaving at the end of April.
New Regional Manager, Dwayne Fuller, took over. He still needs Pete's approval for bundled deals. 15% since Dwayne did not know about the earlier terms.
Presented a rival offer for HVAC maintenance. Carlos Echeverria said 'we assume you are not serious'. 1% via fuel savings. Cold afterwards.
Offered 36 months to Meridian. MD Elena Castro approved 12% off ($49.2k per year) and agreed to cap CPI uplift at 3%. Carlos said stable contracts help them retain technicians.
Added two buildings; 4% off per building. Carlos said the rate is 'already set for 3-year customers'.
Extended to a 5-year renewal. 13% and CPI cap 2.5%, signed by Elena Castro. Carlos notes that 5 years was the first time we met their top of the card.
Offered annual prepay upfront. Naomi Sandoval said it was nice, gave 4%, and said the CRO decides on anything over 8%.
Our CIO called CRO Isaac Moreau. Naomi's original quote of $720k came down 22% ($561.6k). Isaac wanted a case study as part of it.
Rival quote got an 8% revised quote. Naomi said that was the maximum she could grant.
Second call with Isaac. 25% off the expansion, a record. He said they were closing the half-year strongly and he could 'be flexible'.
Tried prepaying again for a 3-year deal. Naomi gave 5%, Isaac not involved.
Asked for a 24-month fixed price on rebar. Walt Dziedzic refused to fix price beyond 90 days and gave no discount.
Committed 6,000 tonnes over two quarters. VP Sales Gary Lindholm gave 7% below mill-plus. Walt said, 'tonnage is what I can sell upstairs'.
Offered net-10. Walt said it helps their credit line but it gave just 2%.
Committed 9,500 tonnes over two quarters. Gary approved 10% under mill-plus pricing, $192k savings. Priced valid for 60 days.
11% off on 12,000 tonnes over 6 months, the best I have seen on the file. Gary said mills are over-supplied now, which helps.
